result.reason: Clarity: B segments the letter under headings so performance, tax activity, tracking error and the fee change are separable, and it glosses the two terms a lay reader would trip on (gross-of-fees, ex-ante tracking error). It frames the fee as a movement from 0.30% to 0.40% rather than leaving the reader to compare two rates. A compresses the harvest, YTD losses, DAF lot reservation and tracking error into a single paragraph and buries the headline return mid-sentence. B's edge is structural, not a function of length. Tone: the notes call for formal address, figures over adjectives, and tax activity in one short paragraph. A opens 'Dear Martin Delahaye' without honorific or trustee capacity, editorialises with 'which we utilized to our advantage' and 'well within', softens the fee news with 'adjusting the advisory fee structure' before conceding it is an increase, and merges tax with tracking error. B uses a full formal block addressed to the trustee, reports flatly, leads with the increase, and holds tax activity to one short paragraph. B's only flaw is the salutation extension to 'members of the Delahaye household', which is wrong for a trust account and should be struck before sending; that is a one-line fix versus several substantive edits needed in A.
